subject.title: Dashboard shows deployment version drift warning

question: Should backend-only or frontend-only production deploys be required to converge immediately to the same SHA, or should the dashboard treat their resulting mismatch as a tolerated rollout state?
rationale: Current main contains both a strict same-SHA deployment invariant and supported single-target deployment modes, so changing warning severity or suppression requires an explicit operational policy choice.

options.title: Require immediate convergence
options.body: Keep the red warning and require each single-target production deploy to be followed by a full same-SHA deployment or documented convergence operation.

options.title: Model partial rollout state
options.body: Record deploy target and timing so recent intentional single-target drift is informational while persistent unexplained drift remains actionable.

options.title: Remove dashboard detection
options.body: Rely on workflow checks and logs, accepting the loss of a user-visible signal for incomplete frontend/backend convergence.

recommendation.title: Require immediate convergence
recommendation.body: Keep the red warning and require each single-target production deploy to be followed by a full same-SHA deployment or documented convergence operation.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the strongest recent history signal across both the deployment workflow contract and current dashboard surface.
